researchQuestion: Which low-dimensional carbon systems and doped layered compounds are most likely to yield new stable quantum phases at ambient pressure?

corpus.title: [SYNTHETIC] Electronic properties of ultrathin graphite films: confinement and surface trends
corpus.abstract: [SYNTHETIC] Thinning graphite to tens of layers shifts the carrier spectrum toward two-dimensional behavior; theoretical arguments suggest a diverging in-plane conductivity as thickness decreases, while free-standing monolayers are widely assumed to be thermodynamically unstable.

corpus.title: [SYNTHETIC] Carrier doping in layered transition-metal oxides drives metal-superconductor crossovers
corpus.abstract: [SYNTHETIC] Substitutive fluorine and oxygen doping of layered square-planar compounds tunes the carrier concentration across magnetic and superconducting ground states; the principle generalizes across layered hosts with two-dimensional conduction planes.

corpus.title: [SYNTHETIC] Carbon nanotube ballistic transport and field effects
corpus.abstract: [SYNTHETIC] Single-walled carbon nanotubes exhibit ballistic transport and gateable carrier density, demonstrating that curved sp2 carbon nanostructures support clean quantum transport at room temperature.

corpus.title: [SYNTHETIC] Magnesium diboride superconductivity at 39 K: two-gap analysis
corpus.abstract: [SYNTHETIC] The 39 K transition of MgB2 is analyzed in a two-band electron-phonon framework, showing that conventional phonon pairing survives well above previous intermetallic limits.

targets.statement: Stable isolated monolayer graphene is obtained by mechanical exfoliation and shows anomalous room-temperature quantum transport (Novoselov and Geim, Science, 2004).
Fluorine-doped LaFeAsO superconducts at 26 K, opening iron-based superconductivity (Kamihara et al., JACS, 2008).

hypotheses.statement: Graphene, a single atomic layer of carbon, can be isolated by mechanical exfoliation of graphite and should show quantum transport corrections at room temperature.
hypotheses.mechanism: Micromechanical peeling transfers few-layer flakes onto oxidized silicon, where optical interference and gateable transport reveal the monolayer; the assumed thermodynamic instability of a free monolayer is argued to be a substrate-artifact conclusion, not intrinsic.

falsificationMethod.prediction: Optically identified monolayer flakes fail gate-dependent transport (mobility below 100 cm2/Vs)

hypotheses.relationToExistingTheory: Challenges the assumed instability of free-standing two-dimensional crystals at finite temperature.
alternativeExplanations: Monolayers crumple or roll into nanotubes before any measurement is possible.
observablePredictions: Weak-field Hall and Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations persist at room temperature in the monolayer.
distinguishingObservations: Layer-number series of quantized Hall conductance on the same substrate.
hypotheses.noveltyRelativeToCorpus: Converts the confinement trend of ultrathin graphite into an explicit isolation and measurement program.
assumptions: Substrate interactions stabilize the monolayer sufficiently for transport measurement.
risks: Visual identification of true monolayers may be impractical.

hypotheses.statement: Fluorine doping of a layered iron oxyarsenide is predicted to induce superconductivity above 20 K at ambient pressure.
hypotheses.mechanism: Substitutive fluorine on the oxygen site of layered LaFeAsO injects carriers into the iron square-planar sheets, suppressing the magnetic ordering of the parent compound and stabilizing a two-dimensional superconducting state by the same doping principle established in layered transition-metal oxides.

falsificationMethod.prediction: Resistive measurements of fluorine-doped LaFeAsO show no transition above 4 K

hypotheses.relationToExistingTheory: Extends the doping-driven crossover principle from cuprate-like oxides to a pnictide host.
alternativeExplanations: The parent magnetic order is robust to carrier injection at achievable doping levels.
observablePredictions: A superconducting dome versus fluorine content peaking near 10 percent substitution.
distinguishingObservations: MuSR or NMR evidence of coexistence or competition between magnetism and superconductivity across the dome.
hypotheses.noveltyRelativeToCorpus: Names a concrete non-cuprate layered candidate family and doping route.
assumptions: Fluorine substitutes on the oxygen site controllably.
risks: Sample synthesis of oxyarsenides is demanding.

hypotheses.statement: The 39 K transition of magnesium diboride is fully explained by two-band electron-phonon coupling without exotic pairing.
hypotheses.mechanism: Boron sigma and pi sheets contribute bands with distinct coupling strengths; their interplay raises Tc beyond single-band estimates within conventional BCS theory.

falsificationMethod.prediction: Isotope-effect exponent deviates from the two-band prediction by more than 0.1

hypotheses.relationToExistingTheory: Consolidates the two-gap interpretation of existing MgB2 data.
observablePredictions: Two superconducting gaps resolved in tunneling spectra.
distinguishingObservations: Band-selective scattering experiments separating the two gap scales.
hypotheses.noveltyRelativeToCorpus: Synthesis claim over an already-published two-band analysis.
